articles.source: Business News Today: Latest Business New
articles.summary: The IMD has issued a weather alert for heavy rain across Tamil Nadu and Puducherry due to a developing depression.
articles.explain: A 'depression' in meteorology is a low-pressure weather system that often leads to strong winds and heavy rainfall. The IMD provides these alerts so that local authorities and citizens can prepare for potential flooding or infrastructure disruptions caused by the storm.

story.title: Severe Weather Alerts and Depression

articles.title: Bajaj Finance said set to launch up to $1.2 billion QIP as early as this week
articles.source: mint - markets
articles.summary: Bajaj Finance is preparing to raise approximately $1.2 billion through a Qualified Institutions Placement (QIP) this week following successful investor roadshows.
articles.explain: A Qualified Institutions Placement (QIP) allows a company to sell shares to a specific group of institutional investors, like mutual funds or insurance companies, rather than the general public. This is a common way for large companies to raise capital efficiently for growth or debt repayment. It matters because it signals confidence in the company's future while potentially diluting existing shareholders' stakes.

story.title: Bajaj Finance QIP Fundraising
story.so_far: Bajaj Finance is one of India's largest non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), providing consumer and small business loans. QIPs (Qualified Institutions Placements) are a mechanism for listed companies to raise capital quickly from institutional investors without the extensive regulatory paperwork of a public follow-on offering.

articles.title: Coinbase, Kalshi join lawsuit backing CFTC over US stock perp futures
articles.source: Cointelegraph.com News
articles.summary: Major crypto firms including Coinbase and Kalshi have filed legal support for the CFTC regarding the regulation of stock-based perpetual futures.
articles.explain: The CFTC is a U.S. government agency that regulates the futures and options markets. 'Perpetual futures' are a type of derivative that allows traders to hold a position indefinitely without the contract expiring. The industry wants the right to offer these on stocks, while regulators are cautious about the risk and jurisdictional oversight required to keep these markets safe.

story.title: Regulation of Stock Perpetuals
story.so_far: The crypto industry has been pushing to expand the types of products available on regulated exchanges. Perpetual futures are complex derivatives that allow traders to bet on the price movement of an asset without an expiration date. There is ongoing conflict between federal regulators and exchanges over who has the authority to approve these types of speculative financial products.

timeline.text: Crypto entities are backing the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) in a legal battle to permit trading of perpetual futures tied to individual stocks.
Additional crypto firms have joined the effort to support the CFTC in the ongoing legal dispute regarding stock-based perpetual derivatives.

articles.title: Coinbase, Kalshi, Kraken parent back CFTC in legal fight over stock perpetual futures
articles.source: CoinDesk: Bitcoin, Ethereum, Crypto News
articles.summary: Kraken joined Coinbase and other industry players in a collective legal filing supporting the CFTC's stance on perpetual stock futures.
articles.explain: By backing the regulator (the CFTC), these exchanges are trying to gain legal clarity that would allow them to offer new, high-risk investment products. These firms argue that allowing these trades on regulated platforms provides transparency, whereas current restrictions might push this volume to less-regulated or offshore markets.

articles.explain: Precious metals are often viewed as safe-haven assets. When interest rates are high, they usually struggle because they don't provide interest income; however, investors look to them as a hedge when they worry about currency devaluation or broader economic instability.

articles.title: Bitcoin short-term holders send 47K BTC to exchanges at a loss
articles.source: Cointelegraph.com News
articles.summary: Bitcoin dropped to an 11-week low as short-term investors sold their holdings at a loss due to prices falling below their average cost.
articles.explain: When Bitcoin's market price drops below the average price paid by recent buyers (the 'cost basis'), it can create 'panic selling' as those investors try to minimize losses. This can create a chain reaction of downward pressure on the price.
